page: Microsoft Azure F16ams_v6 is a memory-intensive virtual machine belonging to the Famsv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor operating at 3.7 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache per core. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. There is no local storage bundled with this instance, though it is premium storage capable, and it does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results indicate strong performance in memory-bound and single-core operations. The server achieves top-tier performance in text generation for small language models, reaching 342.9 tokens per second, and strong performance in prompt processing for small models at 3006.69 tokens per second. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and PassMark memory scores also rank in the top 25%. Standard multi-core CPU performance, memory bandwidth, and database operations fall within the average range.

Given its high memory density of 8.0 GB per vCPU and dedicated AMD EPYC cores, the F16ams_v6 offers a balanced cost-to-resource profile for memory-heavy workloads that do not require local NVMe storage. The lack of integrated local storage represents a tradeoff, requiring external network storage attachments. This server is well-suited for memory-intensive applications, database operations, small-scale language model inference, and memory-cached web serving.
